title: Returned Transfers, Stopped Money and the Loading on a Restoration Charge
content:
Where money sent to a host has come back unpaid, the charge for restoring cover on their Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment carries a loading, and a stop currently standing on the money makes it heavier.

- Where a transfer to the host has been returned unpaid in the twelve months before and money is currently stopped on the host's payout account, the charge carries the marketplace's settlement-risk loading of 1.3 times the figure.
- Where a transfer has been returned unpaid in that period and no money is stopped on the account, it carries the marketplace's returned-transfer loading of 1.15 times the figure.
- Where no transfer has been returned in that period, no loading is carried on that account.

### Condition and result

| Transfer returned unpaid in the twelve months before | Money stopped on the account | Loading |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 1.3 |
| yes | no | 1.15 |
| no | either | none |

A stop standing on the account with no returned transfer in the period carries no loading at all on that account.

### Source of the readings

Returned transfers and whether money is currently stopped are read from the host's Keyturn Host Payout Account, the returned transfers being those recorded on its ledger within the twelve months before. Money is stopped where a ground for stopping it stands recorded against that account, and no such ground means no money is stopped.
